paragraphs: Rabbi Alexandri, after praying, said, etc., Berakhot 17a. He was the teacher of Ahavah, Rav Adda’s father (see there). Rav Acha wished to see him in a dream (see Pappos). “He was in Abaye’s time”—I do not know whence he derives this. Though Abaye says at Ketubbot 77, end of b, “To exclude one who has not fulfilled even a single letter,” this does not prove he was in his generation. It is also unlikely: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi spoke in Rabbi Alexandri’s name, and was Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher; requires examination. Rabbi Alexandri gives several expositions in Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba’s name (Nedarim 41a). He wished to attend to Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa’s burial, Ketubbot, there. In Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name, Berakhot 59a, two things. Yoma 53b: Rabbi Alexandri said, “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi raises a contradiction.” Chelek 98a, two things; there 99b: Rabbi Alexandray said, “Whoever studies Torah for its own sake,” etc.; Rav says, etc.; Rabbi Yochanan says, etc.; Levi says, etc. Jerusalem Talmud, end of Rosh Hashanah: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi in Rabbi Alexandri’s name; Tanchuma, end of Tetze. Rav Mordekhai spoke to him, Yoma, there. This requires examination: Rav Mordekhai was Rav Ashi’s student, much later than Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani in his name, Tanchuma, Behar. Necessarily Rabbi Alexandri, teacher of Ahavah, Rav Adda’s father, is another, since Rav Adda was born when Rabbi died.
